rows.en:
"There's the air-raid shelter in the classroom!"
That's what they said.{p}

Of course, everyone knew about that shelter.
They also knew it was too small for all of them.
They looked at one another.
And the next instant, they all broke into a run at once.
Leaving the injured and the girls behind.{p}
A few of the bigger, faster ones reached the classroom first.{p}

They scrambled over each other to dive into the shelter, then slammed the door shut.
After a short pause, footsteps came closer.
The girls had caught up.
"Open up, please!"
"Help meee!"
The voices came from right above their heads.
But the ones inside the shelter wouldn't open the door.
They knew that if they opened it, everyone would pile in.
And if everyone got in, the place would be useless as a shelter.
They probably wouldn't even be able to close the door anymore.
Better that a few survive than that everyone dies...
With that selfish logic, they kept the door shut.
That was when it happened.{p}

When it had died down, they realized something terrible.
They could no longer hear the voices outside the door.
No... when they strained their ears, they could just barely hear them.
"How could you... how could you..."
"How could you... how could you..."
Thin, reproachful voices.
And pained moaning, too.
It seemed the others outside had been badly hurt.
Even so, they didn't open the door.
Maybe they were scared.
The moment they opened it, there might be another explosion.
They'd managed to get away, so why throw themselves into danger on purpose? That's probably what they thought.{p}

...Of course, it wasn't anything to be proud of.
And their punishment came soon enough.{p}

It started with a smell.
A sharp, acrid smell that stung the nose.
Then came a sound.
Crackle, crackle... crackle, crackle.
There was no mistaking it.{p}
Fire!{p}

The fire must have spread to the rubble.
If they stayed put, they'd be roasted alive.
There was still the danger of bombs, but they made up their minds to get out.
One of them unlocked the door and pushed.
"Huh?"
Something was catching on it, and it wouldn't open.
In a panic, the rest of the guys pitched in.
But it still wouldn't open.
They must have been frantic.
If they didn't hurry, the fire would spread.
But no matter how hard they pushed, the trapdoor wouldn't budge an inch.
"Wh-what do we do?!"
someone screamed, half in tears.
Then, as if in answer, a voice came from above their heads.
"Die in there."
It was a voice that seemed to rise from the depths of the earth.
But it sounded a lot like one of the classmates they'd left behind.
So they begged for help.
"Help us!
Let's escape together!"
Pretty selfish, huh?
Asking the very person they'd abandoned to help them.
But the voice answered coldly.
"That bombing just now hurt me badly.
I can't escape anymore."
"Then we'll carry you on our backs!
So let us out of here☆"
Their desperate cries didn't reach their classmate.
"It's too late..."
Saying only that, she fell silent.
After that, no matter what they said, she never answered again.
Soon, the fire reached the classroom.{p}

By the time the fire was finally out, half the building had burned down.
Of course, every one of the students inside the shelter was dead.
But here's the strange part.
The girls' bodies were lying in a heap on top of the shelter's door.
Most of them had been torn to pieces by the blast, they say.
One look was enough to tell they'd died instantly.
...That's right, do you see it now?
If they died instantly, then who was it that talked to the students in the shelter?
Even with their bodies dead, did their bitter souls still try to take revenge on the traitors?
A while later, the war ended and the school building was repaired.
But rumors started that a ghost appeared in that classroom.
Even though the shelter had supposedly been filled in, and the place exorcised.
The rumors just wouldn't die, so in the end they walled up the whole classroom.
Thinking about it now, that was a pretty crazy thing to do.
But in all the chaos after the war, I guess they got away with it.{p}

"It's a restroom, isn't it?!"
Before {f:I|I} could answer, Hosoda cut in.{p}

Mr. Kuroki grinned.
"That's just like you, Hosoda. Sorry, but you're wrong.
What used to be behind here was something else entirely."
With that, he began his story.{p}

Behind this wall, there was a morgue.
Of course, it wasn't a morgue from the start.
It was originally just an ordinary classroom.
During the war, a lot of people died around here, too.
Ideally, they'd have wanted to give them a proper burial.
But back then, just staying alive took everything you had.
So a lot of people came here to lay their dead, "just until things settle down..." as the excuse went.{p}

The windows were covered with cloth, and in that classroom, dim even at midday, lay a great many corpses.
It couldn't have been a pleasant sight.
One day, a girl was carried in.
Along with a boy who seemed to be her big brother.
A bomb had gotten her, and she was no longer breathing.
So they laid her body in that morgue.
The boy cried and cried, wailing.
It was a terribly tragic accident, but back then it was nothing unusual.
So people quickly forgot about it.
Two or three days later, there was another bombing nearby.
People died that time too.
And they were carried into the morgue.
But the people carrying them saw a figure moving in the dim room.
Apparently there was total, utter panic.
They abandoned the bodies and ran out screaming, every one of them.
Some of them even fainted, I hear.
But of course, a corpse can't come back to life.
It was the brother of the girl brought in a few days before.
He must have really loved his little sister.
Seems he'd never left her side for a moment, staying with her the whole time.
Surrounded by strangers' corpses, too. How he managed that, I'll never know.
People complained, but given the circumstances, they couldn't be too hard on him.
He hadn't meant any harm, and the grown-ups who'd lost their heads were partly to blame too, or so it went.
But even after that, he refused to leave the girl.
That was bad, obviously.
He hardly seemed to be eating, and at this rate he'd die.
So people tried to take him out of the morgue.
But the boy wouldn't have it.
He flailed his thin, pasty-white arms.
People said you'd wonder where a body of nothing but skin and bones got that kind of strength.
He thrashed so hard that nobody could handle him.
In the end, they decided to just leave him be.{p}

A man was walking down this hallway.
By then, the school itself had become something like a hospital and lodging house rolled into one.
He was there for an injury or an illness, and had probably gotten up to go to the toilet or something.
And he passed through this hallway.
The man knew there was a morgue here, too.
It gave him the creeps, so he quickened his pace to hurry past, when suddenly he heard a voice.
A low, mumbling voice.
Without meaning to, he stopped and strained his ears.
It seemed to be coming from the room being used as the morgue.
The man peeked in, ever so carefully.{p}

"...Open your eyes for me... Have you come to hate your big brother...?"
It was that boy's voice.
Realizing it, the man broke out in goose bumps like grains of millet.
The boy was talking to his dead sister.
His longing for her must have finally driven him mad...
That's what the man thought.{p}

So the man hurried back to his bed.
The next day, several grown-ups showed up at the morgue.
They'd heard what the man saw last night and rushed over.
And they tried to drag the boy out of there by force.
They thought separating him from his sister's body was the best thing for him.
But he went on a rampage.
Like a wild beast.
Slipping through the hands of the grown-ups who'd failed to catch him, the boy ran to his sister's side.
And he screamed.
"How could you try to tear us apart?! That's too cruel!
Get up, we have to run☆"
Saying that, he tried to lift his sister up in his arms.
But seeing that her body was still limp, his eyes filled with tears.
"Why won't you wake up★
Is it because you lost so much blood?
If it's blood you need, your big brother will give you some☆"{p}
But the next instant, the knife sank into the boy's own chest.{p}

A moment later, bright red blood sprayed out.
The spatter fell on the girl's small white face, too.
And the boy collapsed on top of his sister.
When the grown-ups came to their senses and checked, he was already dead.
Even after the war ended, it seems no one ever came forward saying they knew them.
Thinking about it now, maybe he'd had a nervous breakdown.
His heart probably wasn't strong enough to live all alone.
In the end, they were buried as unclaimed dead.{p}

But from then on, ghost rumors started up about the classroom that had been the morgue.
Some said it was the ghost of a boy, blood pouring from his chest, searching for his sister.
Others said it was the ghost of a girl who stared at you, still and lonely.
There were all sorts of versions, but they all agreed on one point: there was a ghost.
Around that time, students who had class in that room started collapsing one after another.
So they decided to close the classroom off.
I imagine they really wanted to have it exorcised or rebuilt.
But it was a time when there was nothing to go around.
They couldn't afford luxuries like that.
So they walled it up, passageway and all.
They say the ghost rumors died down after that.{p}

That's right.
Back in here was a staircase, and it led down to a food storeroom in the basement.
During the war, there were shortages of everything, so even food was handed out in fixed daily rations.
That's why the storeroom was always under heavy guard.{p}

Around then, there was a brother and sister who'd been burned out of their home in an air raid and had taken refuge near the school.
The brother was about the age of a high schooler today, and the sister about elementary school age.
The two of them were very close.
They always looked out for each other and kept each other going.
But one day, the sister came down with a fever.
Unlike today, there were no doctors and no medicine.
All the boy could do was cool her forehead with a wet cloth.
Tormented by the fever, the sister began to babble deliriously.
At this rate, she was in danger.
After agonizing over it, the boy hit on an outrageous idea.
He would sneak into the food storeroom and steal food.
Because he thought what his sister needed most right now was nourishment.
The storeroom was guarded by soldiers.
If he got caught, he wouldn't get off lightly.
But the boy knew it was the only way.{p}

And one night, he snuck into the storeroom.
He waited for the soldier on watch to doze off first.{p}

He went down these stairs, the ones that are inside the wall now.
And there he saw something unbelievable.
What do you think it was?
...That's right, an empty storeroom.{p}

There wasn't a scrap of food.
Everyone said there was supposed to be enough food stockpiled here for hundreds of people.
Just then, a flashlight beam lit up the storeroom.
"Who's there?!"
A soldier came in, shouting.
The guy from before must have woken up.
When he spotted the boy, he clicked his tongue.
"So you saw..."
With that, he twisted the boy's arm up behind him.
"As you can see for yourself, there's no food.
That stockpile for hundreds of people is a big fat lie."
The soldier had a sad look on his face.
"This country is running out of food.
But if we said so, everyone would lose the will to fight.
So no one can be allowed to find out."
The soldier shoved him away.
"Whoa!"
Looking down at the boy sprawled on the ground, the soldier slammed the door shut.
A muffled voice came through.
"I'm sorry for you, but now that you know, I can't let you live."
"Y-You can't! I haven't done anything!"
"We'll say you stole the food from this storeroom.
That way, we'll have an excuse for why it's empty."
The boy pounded desperately on the door.
"Please open up!
My sister's lying in bed with a fever!
I have to get back to her☆"
He shouted it again and again.
But no answer came anymore.
In despair, he looked around the room.
The storeroom was a basement.
There was no way in or out but the door.
He wanted to get back to his sister as fast as he could, but there was no way to do it.
She had to be suffering.
If her fever didn't break, she might even die.
The boy ground his teeth.
He even clawed at the floor, trying somehow to escape.
But the hard-packed earth was hopeless against bare hands.
Helpless, he could only wait as time went by.
Hours later, or maybe even dozens of hours later.
The door creaked open.
The soldier he remembered was standing there.
"It's for the nation. Take the blame as the thief."
The soldier bent down and reached out.
At that instant, the boy rammed into him with all his might.
"Augh!"
The soldier went flying.
In that moment, the boy ran out of the storeroom.{p}

He heard the soldier's voice, but he paid it no mind. He rushed to the place where his sister lay.
He looked into her face... and then he knew.
She had already breathed her last.
He must have felt like he'd been shoved off a high cliff.
But he didn't cry.
They say when grief is too great, the tears won't even come.
She was his only sister.
His only family in the world.
How much time passed after that, I wonder.
Slowly, the boy got to his feet.
And he headed for the storeroom again.{p}

That soldier was in the storeroom.
His comrades were there too, along with a soldier who looked like their superior.
The boy charged straight into the middle of them.
He slammed his whole body into the soldier who'd locked him in.{p}

Of course, if it really was a ghost, something like that wouldn't make it disappear.
But the rumors did.
After that, all of a sudden there were no more students claiming to have seen the ghost.
Though a few years later, a different ghost scare started up.
Well, every school has its seven wonders, after all.{p}

"No, I've had enough."
{f:I|I} shook my head.
"{a}{f:|}?"
I'd already heard so many stories today{f:.|, after all.}
I {f:didn't|don't} want to hear any more.
Besides, any of the stories so far could serve as the seventh if it came to that.
And I had a bad feeling, somehow.
It felt like if I stayed here, something bad would happen.
Mr. Kuroki seemed a little deflated.
"I see. Well, if that's how it is, fine.
The good part's actually still to come, you know?"
No matter what he said, {f:I'd|I'd} had enough.
Mr. Kuroki shrugged.
"Then go on home. Be careful."
"Okay... thank you very much."
{f:I|I} bowed.
Hosoda was pouting, clearly unhappy, but he didn't say anything.{p}

It was better this way{f:|}...
{f:I|I} clutched my bag and left the school behind.{p}

All right.
Then let me tell you.{p}

I was in my second year of high school when I heard this boy's story.
Back then, too, the school's seven wonders were all the rage.
There was the dancing skeleton in the science room, the bronze statue that walks alone at night, the music room where blood drips from the ceiling... all kinds of them.
But they were all lies.
Lies somebody cooked up.
But that one story, when I heard it, gave me chills.{p}

That's right.
They said if you pressed your ear against the wall, you could hear agonized moaning.{p}

Back then, I was interested in that sort of thing myself.
When I heard the rumor, I went with a good friend of mine to test our nerve.{p}

It was right around dusk, I think.
In the corner of the dim hallway, just this patch of wall seemed to float there, glowing faintly white.
I had a vaguely bad feeling about it, but having come this far, we couldn't back out.
We pressed our ears against the wall.
...At first, I couldn't really tell.
You know how when you plug your ears, there's a humming, a sound that isn't quite a sound?
It was just like that.
But mixed in with it, I could hear something.
A voice...?
Like someone whispering far away.
To hear it better, I pressed my ear against it so hard it went numb.{p}

I closed my eyes too, to concentrate on my hearing.
Then the voice got louder.
Now it was as if someone were whispering right next to me.
I could even tell it was Japanese.
"Why... why..."
It kept repeating just that one word, over and over.
Was it the voices of the people who died because they weren't let into the shelter?
Or of the people who were roasted alive because they couldn't get out of it?
I felt like I'd been doused with ice water.
Unable to take it anymore, I opened my eyes.{p}

There was a face, right in front of my nose!
An agonized face, rising out of the wall.
It was as if someone were trying to come out.
And it was only about ten centimeters from where I had my ear pressed.
I thought my heart would stop.
I wanted to leap away, but my legs wouldn't move.
Just as I was about to scream...
The eyes of the face in the wall, closed until then, snapped open.{p}

I screamed.
And I fell flat on my backside.
Funny thing, but that was what got my body moving again.
I scrambled to my feet and ran for my life.
Behind me, my friend was shouting something.
But I didn't even look back.
I was just so scared, so terribly scared, all I could think about was getting out of there.{p}

From the next day on, the whole class called me a coward, though.
The friend who went with me claimed not to have seen any face.
According to my friend, I must have been hallucinating.
But it wasn't a hallucination.
Even now, I can say that with absolute certainty.{p}

That's right.
They said if you pressed your ear to the wall, you could hear sad sobbing.
Hear something like that, and you'd want to try it yourself, right?
I went with a friend to try it, too.
And I gently pressed my ear against the wall.
And what do you know, I could hear something like murmuring voices.
I listened as hard as I could, completely absorbed.
That was the moment.
"I'll curse you."{p}

...That's definitely what I heard.
I turned to look at the friend who'd come with me.
His face was white as a sheet.
No, I'm sure mine was the same.
There was no doubt we'd heard the same voice.{p}
Scared, I practically ran all the way home.{p}

The next day, my friend didn't come to school.
At morning homeroom, our homeroom teacher told us.
Late the night before, there'd been a gas explosion at his house.
He was buried alive, and he died just before they could rescue him.{p}

When I heard that, I nearly fainted.
Caught in an explosion and buried alive, of all things.
That was just like the story about what's behind the wall.
So the voice we'd heard the day before really had been aimed at my friend and me.
Then it had to be my turn next.
That's what I thought.{p}

But that night, and the night after, nothing happened.
I hadn't been cursed.
Why only my friend met a fate like that, I don't know.
Did the ghost take a liking to me?
Or did it hate me so much it didn't even want me as one of its own?
Either way, I escaped with my life.
Not that I'm complaining.
After that, I never once walked down that hallway.
Not until I graduated.{p}

Correct.
They said you could hear the sad sobbing of the boy who lost his little sister.
You can imagine what happens when you tell high schoolers a story like that, right?
My friends and I came here to hear the voice, calling it a test of courage.
So, how did it go, you ask?{p}

Of course we didn't hear anything like that.
All sorts of things happened during the war.
A lot of people died, too.
If every one of them came back as a ghost, Japan would be overrun with ghosts.
Well, it was probably a story some guy threw together after hearing a rumor from a teacher or an upperclassman.
...You look let down.{p}

But think about it.
There's no such thing as ghosts.
I was the same way, so I understand wanting to do tests of courage and such.
But give it up.
There are more worthwhile things you can only do now, aren't there?
Like reading books, or club activities.
You understand what I'm saying, right?
"...Yes."
All I could do was nod.{p}

Mr. Kuroki smiled, satisfied.
"Good, then. Now head on home."{p}

Yes, they said you could hear a resentful voice.
I heard that story right after I started at this school.
And I once tried to see for myself whether it was true.
By putting my ear to this wall.
So, what happened, you ask?
I heard it.
A voice like someone groaning.{p}

But then, some time later, there was a class reunion.
That's where I heard the rest of the story about this wall.
It said the voice changed in volume depending on the time of day.
Quiet in the morning, and growing louder and louder as night came on.
Come to think of it, when I heard it, it was still daytime.
If it had been later, I might have been able to make out what that voice was saying.
I'd been plenty scared, but that's what I found myself thinking.
Even after I came to this school as a teacher, I never forgot it.
If I ever got the chance, I meant to try it again.
The sun's already gone down.
If I pressed my ear here now, I wonder what kind of voice I'd hear.{p}Aren't you two curious too?
A little, yes
Not interested at all

"...I am."
{f:I|I} nodded honestly.{p}
Mr. Kuroki gave a pleased smile.{p}
"Thought so. All right, let's give it a try."{p}

When I turned around, I saw Mr. Kuroki pressed against the wall the same way.
Judging by how he was tilting his head, he couldn't hear anything either, {f:I guessed|it seemed}.{p}

Just then, the wall behind Mr. Kuroki's back gave a squishy lurch.
It stretched like rubber, taking the shape of an arm.{p}

"Sir...!"
The instant Mr. Kuroki looked up at {f:my|my} voice...
The arm in the wall seized his head.
Pulling him close as if in an embrace, it slammed him against the wall!
Hitting it that hard might crack his skull.
{f:I|I} caught my breath.
...But there was none of the dull thud I'd expected.
Instead, his head was silently swallowed into the wall.
It was as if the wall had turned into some thick liquid, like potage.{p}

"Mr. Kuroki!"
Hosoda grabbed hold of him in a panic.{p}

{f:I|I} grabbed his arm too and pulled with all my strength.
But he didn't budge an inch.
His hand squeezed {f:my|my} arm.
He was in agony{f:|}.
Couldn't he breathe{f:|}★
{f:I|I} punched the wall.{p}

Wham, a heavy jolt shot through my fist.
It hurt.
It was an ordinary wall{f:|}.
Just a hard wall that couldn't possibly swallow a person.
"What do you want with Mr. Kuroki{f:|}★"
{f:I|I} shouted at whatever unknown thing it was.
Just then, I heard a small voice.
"Big Brother..."
The voice of a little girl.
A faint, lonely voice.
{f:I|I} remembered the story Mr. Kuroki told us earlier.
Was it the dead sister{f:|}★
Was her spirit still searching for the brother death had parted her from{f:|}★
Mr. Kuroki's struggling was growing weaker.
There was no time to think.
{f:I|I} picked up the flashlight lying on the floor and yelled at the wall.
"{f:Your|Your} brother is already dead{f:|}☆
Don't take Mr. Kuroki away{f:|}☆"
I smashed the flashlight against the wall.
Of course, I didn't think that would do anything.
I just thought it might at least make her flinch{f:|}.
But then...{p}

With a sharp crackle, cracks ran through the wall.
Right before {f:our|our} stunned eyes, the wall began to crumble away.
And at last, the long-hidden door of the morgue appeared.
Released, Mr. Kuroki collapsed to the floor.
A translucent girl was clinging to his neck.
Eyes like black hollows.
I couldn't make out her expression, but was this the sister's ghost{f:?|?}
Without a sound, the door opened.
A gaunt boy stood there, alone.
His lips moved slightly.
"Come to me..."
I couldn't hear a voice, but I knew that was what he said.
The translucent girl turned around.
"Big Brother."
She let go of Mr. Kuroki and ran to the boy.
{f:So|Oh,} he was the brother{f:|}.
They'd finally found each other{f:.|.}
The two of them looked happy, somehow.
Hand in hand, they drifted softly into the darkness.{p}

Thank goodness...
Now nobody would hear those voices anymore{f:.|, right?}{p}

Just as {f:I|I} breathed a sigh of relief, Hosoda's sharp voice rang out behind me.
"Mr. Kuroki's...!"{p}

{f:I|I} shuddered.
I {f:had|had} to get home.
What was here wasn't just some ghost.
It was something terribly evil, something wicked{f:|}.
I couldn't stay here.
The flashlight was broken.
But even if I had to feel my way, I {f:had|had} to get home.
Ignoring Hosoda, who'd sunk to the floor, {f:I|I} staggered off.
Shrill laughter rang out from the darkness.
As if looking forward to something about to begin.
Yes...
The night was nowhere near over.{p}

"...I see. All right."
Mr. Kuroki nodded.
"In that case, you two can head home from here.
I'm going to give it a try myself."
"Are you serious?"
{f:I|I} asked, startled.
His face serious, Mr. Kuroki shook his head.{p}

"Of course I am. It's something I've always wanted to know."
Then he flashed me a grin.
"But keep it a secret from everyone else.
I'll keep quiet about you two, too."
{f:I|I} nearly laughed.
Mr. Kuroki wasn't like a teacher at all.
It'd be great to get someone like him as my homeroom teacher in second year.
Thinking that, {f:I|I} answered.{p}
"Yes, I understand."{p}
...With Mr. Kuroki seeing us off, {f:we|we} walked out through the school gate.{p}

By the time I got home, my family had long since finished dinner.
Getting scolded all the while, {f:I|I} wolfed down my meal and dove into my room.
I flopped onto my bed and tried to go back over everything that had happened today.
So much really had happened{f:...|...}{p}
Just then, the phone suddenly rang.{p}

Come on, now.
Didn't I tell you it was students who died here?
There's no way the ghost of some soldier with no connection to it at all would show up.
The story I heard was that if you put your ear to the wall, you could hear voices groaning in pain.{p}
That's right.{p}

But think about it.
Doesn't something seem off?
The one who killed himself was supposed to be a boy, so why would a soldier's ghost show up?
Sure, there must have been soldiers among the victims brought in here.
But it just doesn't fit together, does it?
That alone makes it sound like a pretty phony story.
But I saw it the other way around: that was what made me suspicious.
If it were made up, you could just patch the details together any way you liked.{p}
So if the story came out this half-baked, wasn't it because there was some truth in it somewhere? That's how I figured it.{p}

So I decided to look into it.
First, I decided to see for myself whether a ghost really appeared.
I hid in the shadows.
And I kept a secret watch on this wall.
And then, it showed up.{p}

A man in a military uniform rose up out of nowhere, glowing faintly.
I let out a scream.
The man turned around.
I still remember the look on his face that moment.
It was terrifying, believe me.{p}
His face looked like this...{p}

...No, it was worse than this.
In real life, it was even scarier.{p}

After all, the thing wasn't human.
The man glared at me with horrible eyes.
The pressure coming off him was overwhelming.
I thought he might glare me to death.
I stood there, unable to move, and he spoke to me.
"Whoever has seen my form... I will kill..."
That's what he said.
I went white as a sheet.
To think a tiny bit of curiosity could bring on something like this...{p}
Just then, something stirred in the darkness.{p}

"Waaah★"
Letting out a pathetic cry, Hosoda clung to {f:me|me}.{p}

It was a man in a plain suit{f:|}.
He gave a quick little bow, and his glasses caught the light.{p}

"Geez. You really scared me."
Hosoda said resentfully.
But {f:I|I} was more curious about the rest of the story.
"Mr. Kuroki... but you weren't killed, were you?
I mean, you're right here talking with {f:us|us}."{p}

Mr. Kuroki nodded.
